answer: Neighborhood-density attestation. Each agent samples a sparse random set of peers and records whether they answer within a latency bound, forming a local connectivity kernel. A new identity is admitted only if its neighborhood overlaps the existing graph above a fixed density threshold. Attackers must sustain many distinct, low-latency-correct nodes across the nebula of sampled neighborhoods, paying real bandwidth and uptime per identity. As the graph fills at dawn each epoch, the required overlap rises, so mass registration becomes linearly costly rather than free.
